countries.name: United States

ug.note: College Board 2025-26 averages: public out-of-state US$31,880, private non-profit US$45,000. Many universities charge more, and some charge less.

pg.note: Master's programmes vary a lot. STEM master's often cost more.

living.note: University cost sheets list about US$20,000 to 25,000 including housing, food and insurance. Big cities cost more.

scholarships.t: Merit aid exists but need-based aid for international students is limited.
Many PhD and some master's students get tuition waivers and a stipend.
For Indian students going to the US for master's or doctoral study.

countries.tests: SAT or ACT for undergraduate (many universities make them optional), TOEFL or IELTS for English, GRE or GMAT for some master's programmes.

after.t: F-1 students can work in their field after graduation on OPT for 12 months. STEM degrees can add a 24-month STEM OPT extension, so up to 36 months. Staying longer usually needs an H-1B work visa.
after.verify: US rules changed sharply in 2025 and 2026. USCIS guidance in October 2025 says the US$100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions applies to people outside the US, and does not apply to students already in the US who change status. Court challenges are ongoing. The wage-weighted lottery also changed. Check USCIS before planning.

countries.settle: Settling usually means H-1B, then an employer-sponsored green card. Waits for Indian applicants are long.
countries.salary: US median pay for each career comes from O*NET and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (shown on the careers above). These are US medians for each job, not a guarantee for new graduates. Doctors trained abroad must also pass US licensing (USMLE) and match into a residency; the odds are low.
notes: Indian students are the largest group in the US: 363,019 in 2024/25 (IIE Open Doors 2025), and new enrolments fell 17% in fall 2025.

countries.name: Canada

ug.note: Statistics Canada 2025/26: average international undergraduate tuition C$41,746. Ontario averages C$49,802, Newfoundland and Labrador C$18,867.

pg.note: Statistics Canada 2025/26: average international graduate tuition C$24,028. Newfoundland and Labrador averages C$6,964. Professional master's cost more.

living.note: IRCC asks single applicants to show C$23,448 a year for living costs from 1 September 2026 (C$22,895 before). Real costs depend on the city.

scholarships.t: Most scholarships come from the university. Many are competitive.
Some provinces and universities fund research master's and PhD students.

countries.tests: IELTS or TOEFL for English. GRE or GMAT only for some master's programmes. Applicants need a provincial attestation letter, except master's and PhD students at public institutions from 2026.

after.t: A Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) can last up to 3 years for master's graduates, and for bachelor's programmes of 2 years or more. A language test result is needed. Some programmes are not eligible, so check the programme.
after.verify: Canada capped study permits at about 408,000 in 2026 (155,000 for new students). Field-of-study rules for the PGWP were not confirmed here.

countries.settle: Canadian work experience can count towards permanent residence through Express Entry. Rules and cut-offs change often.
countries.salary: No checked figure yet. Statistics Canada table 37-10-0122-01 has current figures by field. Please check before relying on any number.
notes: Studying in Newfoundland and Labrador is much cheaper than Ontario.

countries.name: United Kingdom

ug.note: UKCISA: international students can expect about £20,000 to £30,000 a year. Medicine and dentistry can be over £50,000.

pg.note: Master's fees are not capped. Most are one year long.

living.note: Student visa maintenance: £1,529 a month in London and £1,171 outside (up to 9 months), for applications from 11 November 2025. Real costs are higher in London.

scholarships.t: Fully funded one-year master's. Needs 2,800 hours of work experience and a promise to return to India for at least 2 years.
For postgraduate study, run by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission.
Many universities offer partial awards to Indian students.

countries.tests: UCAS application for undergraduate. IELTS or an approved English test. Some master's programmes ask for GRE or GMAT.

after.t: The Graduate Route lets graduates stay and work for 2 years (for applications made by 31 December 2026), 18 months (from 1 January 2027), or 3 years for PhD graduates. No job offer is needed.
after.verify: UK immigration rules have been changing every year, including settlement. Check GOV.UK for the rules at the time you graduate.

countries.settle: After the Graduate Route, staying usually needs a Skilled Worker visa, with a salary and employer sponsor.
countries.salary: The median salary of UK graduates in full-time work 15 months after graduating is £30,000 (HESA, 2023/24). Medicine and dentistry graduates have the highest median, £43,749. International graduates earn less on average.
notes: Bachelor's degrees take 3 years in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and 4 in Scotland.

salaryPoints.l: Median, UK graduates in full-time work 15 months after

countries.name: Australia

ug.note: Typical international tuition for bachelor's degrees. Medicine and some specialist degrees cost more.

living.note: The student visa asks single applicants to show A$29,710 a year for living costs. Sydney and Melbourne cost more.

scholarships.t: Many universities offer partial awards to international students.
Limited and mostly for specific countries or regional study. Check eligibility for India.

countries.tests: IELTS, TOEFL or PTE for English. GRE or GMAT for some master's programmes.

after.t: The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) usually allows 2 to 3 years of work after a bachelor's or master's degree. You must be 35 or under when you apply. Fees rose from 1 March 2026.
after.verify: Australia has been limiting international student numbers and changing visas. Check Home Affairs for current rules.

countries.settle: Permanent residence usually goes through skilled migration and needs points, a skilled occupation and sometimes sponsorship. Rules change often.
countries.salary: Australian Graduate Outcomes Survey: the national median full-time salary was A$71,000 for undergraduates and A$96,600 for postgraduate coursework graduates in 2023. A secondary source reports A$77,000 for undergraduates in 2025.

countries.name: Netherlands

ug.note: Average institutional fees for non-EU bachelor's students (Study in NL, 2026). Individual programmes differ.

pg.note: Average institutional fees for non-EU master's students (Study in NL, 2026).

living.note: The IND financial requirement is €1,130.77 a month from 1 January 2026, about €13,570 a year. Amsterdam is much costlier.

scholarships.t: A one-time award for some non-EU bachelor's and master's students. Check current terms.
Several Dutch universities have their own awards for non-EU students.

countries.tests: IELTS or TOEFL for English-taught programmes. Some programmes have limited places and extra selection.

after.t: Graduates of Dutch universities, and of top foreign universities, can apply for a one-year orientation permit (zoekjaar) to look for work, within 3 years of graduating. A skilled migrant permit then needs an employer and a minimum salary.
after.verify: Salary thresholds quoted (about €3,122 a month for former orientation-year holders, €4,357 under 30, €5,942 from 30) come from a university guide, not IND. Check IND.

countries.settle: Skilled migrant status can lead to permanent residence after about 5 years. Dutch language helps a lot for jobs.
countries.salary: No checked figure yet. CBS (Statistics Netherlands) and Nuffic have current figures. Please check before relying on any number.

countries.name: Germany

ug.note: Most public universities charge no tuition to international students, only a semester contribution (about €150 to 350). Baden-Württemberg has charged non-EU students about €1,500 a semester (check). Private universities charge €5,000 to 20,000 or more.

pg.note: Same as undergraduate. Many English-taught master's programmes are listed in the DAAD database.

living.note: The blocked account amount for the student visa is €11,904 a year (€992 a month) in 2026. Big cities cost more.

scholarships.t: The main German scholarship body, with many programmes for master's and doctoral study.
A small monthly award for high achievers at German universities.

countries.tests: Many bachelor's programmes are taught in German, so a German language certificate is needed (B2 to C1). English-taught master's programmes ask for IELTS or TOEFL. Indian applicants usually need an APS certificate, and many need a foundation year (Studienkolleg) for undergraduate study.

after.t: Graduates of German universities can stay up to 18 months to look for a job in their field, and can work any job during that time. The EU Blue Card needs a job paying at least €50,700 a year in 2026 (€45,934.20 for shortage occupations and recent graduates).
after.verify: Blue Card thresholds come from EY and other advisers. Confirm on the official portal. The Baden-Württemberg fee and the APS and Studienkolleg points were not confirmed today.

countries.settle: A Blue Card can lead to permanent residence in about 21 to 27 months with good German, or 33 months otherwise. Check current rules.
countries.salary: Typical graduate starting pay is about €45,000 to 56,000 a year (secondary estimate). Check Destatis.
notes: Germany is the cheapest option here for a master's degree in engineering and computing, but learning German matters for work.

countries.name: China

ug.note: Bachelor's tuition at one university on the CSC page is about ¥13,800 to 14,600 a year. Other guides give wider ranges.

pg.note: Master's tuition from about ¥15,400 at some universities to ¥72,000 in guides.

living.note: Roughly ¥2,000 to 5,000 a month depending on the city. The CSC stipend (¥2,500 to 3,500 a month) is a rough benchmark.

scholarships.t: Full award: tuition, accommodation, medical insurance and a monthly stipend (¥2,500 undergraduate, ¥3,000 master's, ¥3,500 doctoral).
Many Chinese universities offer partial awards.

countries.tests: Many programmes are in Chinese, and need an HSK result. English-taught programmes exist. Undergraduate scholarship applicants must take the CSCA test in 2026.

after.t: Staying to work usually needs a job offer and a work permit. Settling in China is uncommon for foreign graduates.
after.verify: Not checked on an official source. Most Indian students go to China for medicine.

countries.settle: Permanent residence in China is very rare. Treat China as a place to study, not to settle.
countries.salary: Not covered. Pay depends heavily on the city and the employer.
notes: Medicine abroad (China and elsewhere): to practise in India you must have NEET, a course of at least 54 months plus a 12-month internship, English-medium teaching, all at the same foreign institution, a licence to practise in that country, and then pass the FMGE (until NExT starts). Check the NMC website before choosing a university.

countries.name: Singapore

ug.note: NUS 2026/27 reports: about S$21,400 to 22,200 with the MOE Tuition Grant, about S$33,400 to 39,700 without it. Medicine about S$87,800 with the grant.

living.note: Roughly S$1,000 to 2,000 a month. Housing is the largest cost.

scholarships.t: Lowers tuition, but you must work in Singapore for 3 years after graduating (the bond).
Partial or full awards for strong applicants.

countries.tests: Indian board marks and SAT, A-level or IB scores, depending on the university. IELTS or TOEFL for English.

after.t: Graduates need an Employment Pass to work. In 2026 the minimum qualifying salary is S$5,600 a month for most sectors (S$6,200 in financial services), rising to S$6,000 and S$6,600 from 1 January 2027. Candidates must also pass the COMPASS points test.

countries.settle: Permanent residence is possible but competitive, and not guaranteed.
countries.salary: Fresh graduates from the local universities had a median gross monthly salary of S$4,500 in 2025 (NUS S$4,746, NTU S$4,550, SMU S$4,747). NUS Computing graduates earned a median of S$6,400. Note: the local graduate median (S$4,500) is below the Employment Pass minimum (S$5,600), so a foreign graduate needs a better-than-median offer to stay.
notes: Employers know the NUS, NTU and SMU names well, so competition for places is high.

fieldNotes.health: Doctors, dentists, nurses and pharmacists must pass the licensing exams of the country they work in (for example USMLE in the US, PLAB in the UK, MCCQE in Canada, AMC in Australia). That takes extra years. Studying medicine abroad can be much harder than studying a master's in public health or biotechnology. Medicine abroad does not follow the 4 + 2 pattern, so we do not show a rough total for it.
fieldNotes.sci: Research careers abroad usually go through a PhD, which is often funded. Master's degrees can lead to industry jobs.
fieldNotes.eng: Engineering master's degrees are the most common route abroad. Professional registration (such as PEng in Canada) comes later.
fieldNotes.tec: Computing and data are the most common fields for work abroad after a master's degree. Visa rules matter more than the degree.
fieldNotes.com: Finance and accounting qualifications are country-specific. A CA from India is recognised in some countries through agreements, but you will usually need exams or a local qualification.
fieldNotes.des: Design degrees abroad depend on a strong portfolio. Architecture needs local registration after the degree.
fieldNotes.psy: Practising as a psychologist abroad needs a local licence, which takes years. Research and user experience careers move more easily.
fieldNotes.law: An Indian law degree does not qualify you to practise abroad. A master's in law and a local bar exam are normally needed (for example the SQE in England and Wales).
fieldNotes.media: Media and teaching careers abroad usually need strong local language skills and local teaching certification.
fieldNotes.pub: Public service and defence careers are tied to the Indian state. Study abroad mainly helps in policy, research and international organisations.
fieldNotes.hos: Hospitality and aviation have local licensing. Switzerland and similar countries have well-known hospitality schools, but they are costly.
fieldNotes.spo: Sports science and coaching degrees exist in most of these countries. Athletic scholarships exist mainly in the US.
fieldNotes.agr: Agricultural science master's programmes are strong in the Netherlands, Germany and Australia. Veterinary degrees must be re-validated in each country.
fieldNotes.voc: Skilled trades are in demand in Germany, Canada and Australia, mostly through apprenticeships and skilled-worker visas rather than university study.
fieldNotes.arts: Performing arts careers abroad depend on auditions and portfolios. Visas for artists differ from student visas.
fieldNotes.mar: Maritime careers use international licences (STCW), which makes them easier to move across countries.

routes.name: Bachelor's and master's abroad
lines: Start after Class 12, so you apply in Class 12 or earlier.
Costs the most overall, since you pay for 4 to 6 years abroad.
You build a local network, and a longer stay can help with work visas and settling.
Entry tests: SAT or ACT (US), UCAS (UK), IELTS or TOEFL, and sometimes aptitude tests.
Total cost depends heavily on the country and university. Compare the cards below before deciding.

routes.name: Bachelor's in India, master's abroad
lines: Do a 3 or 4-year degree in India, then apply for a master's abroad in the last year.
Costs less overall. The Indian degree is cheap, and you pay abroad for only 1 to 2 years.
Entry tests: GRE or GMAT for some programmes, and IELTS or TOEFL.
Check that your Indian degree length is accepted: some countries and programmes prefer 4-year degrees.
Some students find work and settle abroad this way, but it is never guaranteed. Visa rules, job markets and your field all matter.
If you borrow for fees, work out how you would repay the loan if you do not get a job abroad.

legend.official: Read from an official or government page on the date shown.
legend.secondary: From a news, university or education site. Treat as a guide.
legend.estimate: Our estimate from general knowledge. Not checked on the date shown.

disclaimer: Figures are ranges from public sources, checked on 21 Oct 2026. Fees, visas and settlement rules change often, and some figures here are estimates. Always check the official site for the university and the country before deciding. This is not immigration or financial advice. Borrowing for study abroad is a serious commitment. Settling abroad is never guaranteed.
